items.response:
Fun, congrats on the beta wrapping up. I don't have your office location or any dietary needs for the group saved, so I'll work from what I can find and flag gaps rather than guess. I'll look for places that take a group of 8 next Thursday.
Action: Search for restaurants near the office that can seat 8 at lunch next Thursday, shortlist three with availability and menu options, and send them to you before booking anything.

I don't have your recurring charges, the Amazon batteries order, or a full usage history in front of me, so I won't guess at them. What I can see from this conversation: the Saturday run is on the calendar, internet is Bell Fibe at $95 a month, the PRD skeleton is in Notion, your Vancouver flight preferences are saved, and the week's to-do list is pulled together.
Action: Check your bank and card statements for automatic monthly payments other than bills, look up the Amazon batteries order status, and put together a history list for you.

Partly. Written Portuguese is easy to read with Spanish, and you'll catch a lot of signs and menus, but spoken Portuguese (especially in Portugal) sounds quite different, so understanding people and being understood is harder than reading. Most people in tourist areas will switch to English or meet you halfway if you start in slow Spanish, but learning a few Portuguese basics will go a long way.
Action: Draft a one-page cheat sheet of essential Portuguese phrases and pronunciation traps for your Lisbon trip and save it to your notes.

From what I have, your blocks are: Thu 10 Dec, leave at 5:00 pm for Leo's winter concert (you've already told Tom), and OOO from Mon 21 Dec through Fri 1 Jan, since your flight to Lisbon leaves Sun 20 Dec and you land back in Toronto Sat 2 Jan, so you'd be back Mon 4 Jan. Not sure whether you want Fri 18 Dec (Leo's last school day) marked as well. I don't have what Leo means by 'that thing' from last winter, so I'll look instead of guessing.
Action: Add those blocks to the team calendar once you confirm the 18 Dec question, and search last winter's calendar, photos and notes around the school closure day for what you did.

Ha, 'obviously' is the best part. Dinosaur-shaped pizza dough is basically a career plan. Glad you're home and got that dinner.
Action: Save Leo's paleontologist-and-pizza-chef line to your notes, unless you'd rather I didn't.

Happy to help with both. One constraint I have: Sam gets migraines from strong fragrances, so I'll skip scented gifts like candles, soaps and perfume. I don't have Sam's birthday or your anniversary date in front of me, so I'll check the calendar first, then suggest a gift and a celebration plan and set an early anniversary reminder so it's not the last week.
Action: Check the calendar for both dates, then send you three unscented gift ideas, two ways to celebrate, and a reminder for the anniversary a few weeks out.

Dishwasher pods and paper towels are household staples, so I'll reorder them without asking, the pods as the same Finish Quantum 82 count from Canadian Tire on the TD Visa as last time. A cordless Dyson will probably be well over $150, so I'll find options and ask you before buying. I'll check your order history for your usual paper towel brand rather than guess.
Action: Place the pod and paper towel reorders, and send you two or three cordless Dyson models (the one Hannah has, if I can find out which) with prices for your yes.

I don't have Biscuit's birth date or any behavioural notes saved, so I won't make them up. His old vet records or adoption papers should have the birth date, and for the behaviour box, a few lines from you on anxieties, triggers, how he is with other dogs, and handling will do.
Action: Search your email and notes for his vet and adoption records to find the birth date, and I'll draft the behavioural notes from what you tell me.

Priya is your McGill best friend, and since you both love mysteries, a hardcover Tana French is a safe bet, though I'd check she hasn't already read it. Draft card: 'Priya, a good mystery for a good friend. So glad you're coming. Love, Riya.'
Action: Look up hardcover Tana French titles in stock at local bookstores with prices, and bring you the best option to approve before I order.

On it. I'll write a 15-item spring cleaning checklist into your notes. For the couch, I need to know whether it fits through the basement stairs as is and what day works, so I'll find removal options and quotes rather than guess.
Action: Save the checklist to Notes, and search for couch pickup or junk removal services nearby with prices and available dates.

Good idea, Zoom will be easier for her than WhatsApp video. I'll set it for your usual Sunday call, 9:00 pm Toronto time, which is 6:30 am Monday in Mumbai, before her morning walk, and put both times in the message.
Action: Create the Zoom link for Sunday 9:00 pm Toronto / 6:30 am Monday IST and text it to your mom on WhatsApp with both times and a one-line 'tap this to join'.

Sure. I'll look for upper-intermediate Spanish grammar books with a focused subjunctive section, plenty of exercises, and an answer key. Before ordering, I'd like you to see the options and price, and you could also ask Carlos if he has a preferred one.
Action: Shortlist two or three subjunctive-focused grammar books with price and delivery time, then order whichever you pick.

Here's one line: 'Happy birthday, Tom! Thanks for being such a steady, supportive manager. Hope today is a good one.' It's warm, no age jokes, and short enough for the card.
Action: Tweak the wording if you'd like it different, otherwise it's ready for you to write in the card.

I'm sorry, Riya. Four years tomorrow is a big day, and lighting the diya at home sounds right. I'll make the day gentle.
Action: Pull up tomorrow's calendar, send you a short list of what I'd decline, move or keep (nothing sent to anyone until you say yes), and keep the evening completely clear.

Pros of a four-day week: better retention and recruiting, often equal or better focused output, lower burnout and sick days, and a real perk that costs little. Cons: compressed hours can mean longer days, coverage and client-response gaps, harder scheduling for meetings, and it can quietly turn into five days of work in four if scope doesn't shrink. A trial period with clear metrics usually answers the doubts.
Action: Turn this into a short, friendly message you can send to Priya, and add a few questions her firm should answer before deciding.

Sweet idea. Sam drinks oat-milk flat whites and dislikes anything hazelnut-flavoured, so I'll make sure the order has an oat-milk flat white and a snack with no hazelnut. I'll check that the school front office accepts deliveries to Room 214.
Action: Order an oat-milk flat white and a simple snack for delivery to Riverdale Collegiate Institute, Room 214, around 3:30, and confirm the drop-off works with the school.

Here's an Ellie-friendly version: dogs are descended from wolves, and wolves howl to say 'I'm here, where are you?' A fire truck's siren sounds just like a giant howling dog, so Biscuit is answering it, not being naughty. He's basically singing along with the loudest dog he's ever heard.
Action: Save this to your notes so you have it ready to tell Ellie tomorrow.

Sorry, that's a stressful one for Hannah. In general, she should find out which tow yard has the car (the City, the parking authority or police non-emergency line can tell her from the plate), then bring photo ID, proof of ownership and insurance, and pay the tow and any storage fees there. She can also dispute the parking ticket afterwards if the sign was unclear. I don't want to quote a figure from memory because fees change.
Action: Look up the current Toronto towing, impound and storage fees and the exact retrieval steps, and send you a summary to pass on to Hannah.

Here's the checklist for today: 1) Fix Leo's bike chain. 2) Hang the hallway mirror: tape the spot, find the stud, then use two #10 x 3 in screws into the stud, or two snap toggles or a French cleat if no stud (about 15 kg on plaster-and-lath, so don't use light anchors). 3) Sort the garage recycling. 4) Plant the tomato seedlings. 5) Find the good extension cord. For the mirror you'd need Home Hardware on Queen St E for snap toggles ($9.49), a French cleat kit ($24.99) and painter's tape ($6.99), so check their holiday hours.
Action: Put the checklist in your notes with the Home Hardware items as a first stop.

That spiral is really common, and you're probably right that it's a dying phone, but it makes sense to want to know. A few easy things: try a WhatsApp or video call instead of a regular call, text someone near her who could pop in, and send her a short, no-pressure message so she sees something when the phone is back on.
Action: Set a reminder to try her again in an hour, and draft a short message you can send if you want me to.

Eight already, how! I'll check whether Wonder Workshop on Queen East runs parties for twelve kids and what a Saturday 23 Jan party costs. I won't book anything without you.
Action: Look up Wonder Workshop's party packages, capacity for 12 kids, pricing, and availability for Sat 2027-01-23, and send you the summary.

That sounds like a lovely weekend, but five stops plus leaving at 8 is a lot for one Saturday, and since Sam's driving, I'd plan the winery tastings around that. I'd suggest we sort stops by location and opening hours and move one or two (maybe the lavender farm or the cheese shop) to Sunday so Saturday isn't a sprint.
Action: Draft a realistic Saturday itinerary and a light Sunday, checking opening hours for each stop, and send it for your OK before booking anything.

I don't have Carlos's email in front of me, so I can't judge it yet. Once I've read it I'll compare cost, schedule and format against your current lessons and tell you whether it's worth it or overkill.
Action: Open Carlos's email, summarize the winter intensive (price, schedule, what it adds), and give you a straight recommendation.

Here's a start for this week: book the furnace service (last one in your records is 2023-09, so it's due) and an eavestrough cleaning (last done 2024-10), test the sump pump (replaced May 2024) and check the back-wall strip of the basement that gets damp, and make sure someone's home for the cabinet delivery on Thu 16 Oct, 8:00-10:00. I'd also add smoke and CO detector batteries and sealing drafts.
Action: Save this list to your notes and request quotes for the furnace service and eavestrough cleaning for after you're back Monday.

Happy to. I don't have the dates you'll be away in July, and I don't want Hannah to block the wrong days. Draft: 'Hi Hannah, you kindly offered to help with Biscuit a while back. Would you be able to feed and walk him while we're away from [dates]? We'll pay you, of course. No worries at all if it doesn't work.'
Action: Wait for the dates from you, then send the text to Hannah.

I don't have a record in front of me of you buying the furnace filters, so I'd rather check than guess.
Action: Search your email receipts, order history and notes from before Christmas for furnace filters and tell you whether they were bought, delivered or picked up.

I don't have that episode saved in what I can see now, so I can't name it without guessing.
Action: Search my past summaries and your notes for the developer-platform pricing episode and send you the title and link to forward to Aisha; if I can't find it, I'll ask what show it was from.

Sending the text to Rui now, as drafted. Saturday the 14th for four is probably a busy night, so I'll aim for places with room for a table of four and walkable from home in Leslieville or Riverside, with a preferred time to be confirmed.
Action: Send the snow removal text, then find three walkable restaurants in Leslieville/Riverside with a table for four on Sat 14th and send them to you before booking.

I haven't opened the doc yet. One thing I know that you may need to fix in it: on 2026-05-14 you decided to move same-day CAD-USD settlement from Instant Payouts v1 to v1.1, and PAY-1390 (Jonah) may still be in Sprint 21 scope when it should be in the v1.1 backlog.
Action: Open the Instant Payouts readiness doc in Notion and list unresolved comments, linked tickets, and anything left from last review, flagging PAY-1390 and whether the doc reflects the 2026-05-14 decision.

Lovely idea. I don't have the story of how you two met saved, and the best callback depends on it. In the meantime, a simple option is a short letter swap about first impressions over dessert, or recreating the food or music from back then.
Action: Wait for you to tell me how you met, then turn the best idea into a plan with a shopping list, timed for after Leo's asleep.

Both are in my notes. Running: your first half marathon, the Toronto Waterfront Half Marathon (21K) on 2025-10-19, official chip time 2:04:37; it's the only half on record, so that's your PB unless you've run a faster one. Property tax: paid by pre-authorized debit from the TD joint account (****4471).
Action: Fill in both forms with those answers and show you the entries before I submit anything.

Checklist for Leo's passport renewal: his current passport, completed child application form, two passport photos (still on your to-do), proof of citizenship such as his birth certificate (born July 17, 2019), guarantor and reference details, parent ID and signatures, and the fee. I'll confirm the exact requirements and processing time against the official site before you rely on this, since his passport expires in January.
Action: Save the checklist to your notes and look up the nearest passport appointments or walk-in options, then send you the earliest times.

Here's the lemon loaf in grams: flour 1 1/2 cups is about 190 g, sugar 1 cup about 200 g, butter 1/2 cup about 115 g, plain yogurt 1/2 cup about 120 g, lemon juice 2 tbsp about 30 g, baking powder 1 tsp about 4 g. Those are standard conversions, so they may be off by a few grams depending on how you scoop the flour.
Action: Save this converted recipe to your notes.

I can draft the text, but I don't have Biscuit's feeding amounts, walk routine, or the drop-off time, and I don't have the fire truck backstory saved, so I won't make those up. Draft: 'Hi Hannah, thanks so much for taking Biscuit tomorrow morning. I'll bring him by around [time], with his food and leash. He may get loud if a siren goes by. We'll be back [time].' When you say 'leaving at 5', do you mean 5 am?
Action: Search your notes and messages for the fire truck incident, then fill in the blanks with you and send the text to Hannah.

Got it, shorter replies from here on. Still waiting on what's worked best for your Spanish so I can set up tonight's practice.
Action: Keep replies brief today and build tonight's Spanish practice once you tell me what works for you.

Welcome back, and a board-game do-over for your 10-year anniversary is a great idea. I'll keep it to a Saturday, since Sam is usually marking lab reports on Sunday evenings. I'd look at a board-game cafe or a dinner with a game afterwards, ideally something that nods to the game night where you met.
Action: Check both calendars for open Saturdays, then shortlist three board-game-themed date options and send them for you to pick.

A dinosaur it is. I'll look for a size 7 costume under $50 that will arrive before Friday 30 Jan, and confirm delivery dates so it isn't late.
Action: Search size 7 dinosaur costumes under $50 with delivery before Fri 30 Jan, and order the best-reviewed one that arrives in time.

Will do, tentative. The week of Mon 15 Mar is blocked as you described: prep Mon/Tue, offsite Wed/Thu, and the deck due on Fri 12 Mar. I'll check for clashes first.
Action: Create tentative calendar entries for Fri 12 Mar 'roadmap deck due', Mon 15 to Tue 16 Mar prep, and Wed 17 to Thu 18 Mar Q1 2027 roadmap offsite, and tell you if anything conflicts.

Glad it landed. Riya the poet has a reputation to keep.
Action: Nothing needed, but I can save a Friday haiku for later if you'd like another.

Poor Sam. For Grace and Daniel, unscented is easy: for Grace, who still teaches piano, a nice music-related gift or good treats, and for Daniel, a retired civil engineer, a book on local history or bridges. I'd avoid candles, soaps and anything perfumed.
Action: Look up what's open tomorrow in Ottawa near the Glebe and Alta Vista and send you two gift options for each of them to pick up.

I don't see a text from Nate yet in what I have, so I'll check your messages and email rather than guess, and I won't call him since he prefers texts. Related deadlines to keep in mind: countertop material, colour and edge profile need confirming with his fabricator by Tue 7 Jul 2026 (templating Thu 9 Jul, 8:00-10:00), and Barzotti wants the final cabinet hardware choice by 2026-03-09.
Action: Check your texts and email for Nate's schedule message and report back, and remind you about the countertop choice if it's still not recorded.

Got it, short replies today.
Action: Keep everything brief until 5 and only flag what's urgent.

I don't have the saree link's contents in front of me, so I'll open it and check rather than guess. I'll show prices in CAD, with the original currency in brackets if it's listed in another currency, and compare it to similar sarees to say whether it's fair or tourist pricing. I won't buy anything without asking you first.
Action: Find your saved Kanchi Silks link, pull the price and convert to CAD, and compare it against a few similar listings.

I don't have either answer to hand, and I don't want to guess numbers or times. I'll look up Tom's calendar for the day in February you were trying to find time, and check the May sync log for the amount of Sam's school stuff that came across.
Action: Look up Tom's open slots on that February day and the item counts from the May sync, and send you both; I may need you to confirm which date in February.

Sorry about the heel. You had plantar fasciitis in early 2026, mild and much better since, so the physio should hear that history, and Marcus's calf stretches worked then, so they might help in the meantime. I'll look for after-work or Saturday slots next week.
Action: Find physios with after-work or Saturday availability next week, and send you the options, including which foot, before booking.
